lesson_title: Wall, Staircase, Floor: The Three Numbers of Every Straight Line
hook_text: Every straight line hides three numbers. Find them in order, wall, staircase, floor, and you can describe any line in a test.
clip_script: Picture the vertical axis as a wall and the horizontal axis as the floor. A straight line crosses the wall once, crosses the floor once, and has one steepness in between. Three numbers. Wall first: where the line touches the wall, x is zero. For y equals 2x plus 1, put x equal to zero and get 1. That is the y-intercept, the taxi's starting fee. Staircase next: pick two grid corners on the line, from 0 semicolon 1 to 2 semicolon 5. Up 4, across 2. Up over across is 2. That is the gradient, the rate, R12 a kilometre on a taxi meter. Downhill means negative. Floor last: on the floor, y is zero. 0 equals 2x plus 1 gives x equals negative a half. That is the x-intercept, and a fraction is fine. Wall, staircase, floor. Write each one as a pair with the zero showing and you will never swap them.
visual_style: A whiteboard room with a wall and floor; a line slides in and touches the wall with a glowing dot, a staircase of 2 up for 1 across animates along it, then the floor crossing glows; three numbers stamp into y equals mx plus c.
pacing: Three beats of equal length, one per feature, with the pair notation closing each.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for gradients from any two points and the error museum.
